findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: The back door of the establishment was observed propped open upon arrival. The PIC mentioned that the facility baked cookies earlier in the morning and the door was propped open to allow fresh air inside. The door was closed to correct the violation. Ensure that outer doors are never propped open, unless there are effective methods to prevent the entry of unwanted pests and insects.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(D) Outer Openings, Protected. (D) Except as specified in (B) and (E) of this section, if the windows or doors of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, or of a larger structure within which a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT is located, are kept open for ventilation or other purposes or a TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT is not provided with windows and doors as specified under (A) of this section, the openings shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) 16 mesh to 25.4 mm (16 mesh to 1 inch) screens; (2) Properly designed and installed air curtains to control flying insects; or (3) Other effective means.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the hand sink in the bathroom to be lacking both paper towels and hand soap during the inspection today. The hand sink was immediately stocked during the inspection. Corrected on site. Ensure that hand sinks are always stocked with paper towels and hand soap to facilitate proper hand washing. No follow-up required at this time. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
The handles of scoops located in the sugar and powdered drink mix containers were observed to be stored within the food itself which promotes bare-hand contact with food items. Handles stored in foods must be stored with the handle up and out of the food. Ensure that all in-use utensils are stored properly at the next routine inspection. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 A certified food manager was not present upon arrival of inspector. The manager on duty with certification was on break, and the employee working did not have certification. CFM came back from break and noted they were the PIC to oversee operations until close of business today. Ensure a CFM is on-site during all hours of food service and operation. **See general comments for additional information)
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee was observed going between tasks and did not wash hands between operating the cash register at the order window and handling clean dishes at the 3 part sink. While moving the dish rack at the 3 part sink a utensil was loose and handled to be placed back in the rack. Employee was advised on handwashing between tasks, especially after working the service window and prior to doing anything with clean dishes, single service articles, or food prep/handling. Employee washed hands prior to continuing with the next task.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 1. Mold was observed on the lower edges of the baffle in the ice machine bin, with some surfaces in direct contact with ice. Ice was removed to allow for cleaning. Sanitizer was used to wipe down surfaces where mold was observed while using a baking pan as a barrier between the baffle and ice below. Additional layer of ice was also removed after cleaning. Cleaning and maintenance were discussed. 
2. Approximately a half dozen fruit flies were observed around the mixer, with some of them sitting on cutting boards. Manager noted cookies were made earlier in the day, and the area in question probably needs some additional cleaning. Cutting boards were removed to be cleaned and sanitized. 
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Portions of chicken salad located in a bag dated 10/27 in the fridge door had surface temperatures above 45F. Internal temperatures were observed at 49F-51F. Portions of chicken salad (4) were discarded during inspection. **See general comments for additional information**
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.citation_text:
3-501.19 Open containers of half and half and almond milk were observed in the fridge. One container of half and half had a time stamp of 12:15 and was observed with an internal temperature of 43F. The other containers of half and half and almond milk did not have time stamps and dispensed portions had internal temperatures of 52F and 59F respectively. Half and half and almond milk without time stamps that were placed back in the fridge after being held at room temperature were discarded. Portion of half and half with 12:15 time stamp was removed and placed on the prep table for use. Other milks and whipped topping removed from cold holding were observed labeled with the time and left on prep table for use during inspection. Ensure foods are properly labeled and used or discarded within 4hrs. Cease the practice of placing time controlled TCS foods back in the fridge. **See general comments for additional information**
If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (1) the food shall have an initial temperature of 41F/below when removed from cold holding or 135F/above when removed from hot holding; (2) the food shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control; (3) the food shall be cooked and served, served at any temperature if ready-to-eat, or discarded, within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control; and (4) food in unmarked containers or packages, or marked to exceed a 4-hour limit shall be discarded.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Probe thermometer was used to check chicken salad and was not registering near temperatures observed with inspector’s digital probe thermometers. Ice water solution was used to check accuracy, and facility’s thermometer was observed at 40F. Thermometer was calibrated to 32F with pliers used to adjust the needle. Ensure all thermometers are calibrated to verify accuracy.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-404.14 Damp wiping cloths were observed sitting on counters. One wiping cloth was dipped in sanitizer at 3 part sink to wipe tables. Sani-buckets were emptied and fresh solutions not yet provided. Quat solutions at 200ppm were prepared to allow for proper storage of wiping cloths between uses.
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Wall behind washer/dryer and handsink had areas of disrepair and spots where gaps were present along drywall seams. Owner has plans to repair the wall/remodel the facility. **See general comments for additional information**
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.06 Employee working at the time of inspection did not have a food handler certification and confirmed they have not yet completed the course. Employee stated they were new as of July. PIC was advised on the time frame for certification. Ensure all staff that are not CFMs complete food handler certifications within 30 days of hiring. 
All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 One of the food employees working at the time of inspection did not have a signed reporting agreement on file. Kitchen manager had the employee go over the health policy and sign a copy of the reporting agreement during the inspection. Revised versions of employee health documents were provided on new letterhead with updated reference to 2017 FDA Food Code, and additional copies of the reporting agreement were provided. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 Written procedure with specific actions to be taken in case of a vomit and/or diarrhea incident was not available. Norovirus disinfection handout was provided. Bleach is available for use. Maintain the norovirus disinfection policy on-site along with all other employee health documentation.
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 PIC began drying hands with dispensed paper towels, shut off the manual faucet with paper towels, and then finished drying hands with the same paper towels. Proper technique was discussed. Ensure hands are thoroughly dried prior to using the paper towels to shut off the faucet. Once paper towels are used to shut off the faucet they are contaminated. Get new paper towels to finish drying hands if additional drying is needed after using paper towels to shut off the faucet. Use of forearm or elbow to shut off the faucet is also acceptable.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114  Quat solution at 3 part sink was observed at 100ppm, and sani-buckets were observed near 0ppm. Quat solution at 3 part sink was made within the last 20-30 minutes, so additional chemical was added to bring the concentration to 200ppm. Sani-buckets and solution for espresso machine were remade at the same time. Ensure solutions are maintained at proper concentration.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Change out sanitizer solutions frequently/as needed throughout the operating day. Maintain solutions at 200-400ppm as indicated on label directions, and use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15 Weather strip along lower left side of outer door was damaged. Light was visible along the lower let side of the door. Provide repairs to properly seal the door. 
Outer openings of a food establishment shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Floor drain under 3 part sink is heavily soiled down inside with black buildup some of which appeared to be mold and debris. Drain needs to be thoroughly cleaned and maintained clean to help minimize potential food source for flies and other pests. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Wall behind washer/dryer and handsink had areas of disrepair and spots where gaps were present along drywall seams. Repair and seal the wall.
-Low lying spot was observed in the floor on the left side of the mop sink. Moisture and debris accumulation were present in the area. Provide repairs to seal the low lying spot to eliminate moisture and debris accumulation. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16 Wet mop was observed in the basin of the mops sink. Proper storage was discussed with the option of spreading out the mop head along the top edge of the bucket. PIC repositioned the mop during inspection to allow for proper drying. 
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.06 Employees did not have proof of food handler certification. Laminated list of certified food handlers posted by the handsink and certifications available for staff were expired (course taken in April 2018). All staff that are not certified food managers need to have food handler certifications, and copies of food handler certifications need to be maintained on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC at time of inspection was not a certified food manager. Employee was advised on the requirement for a designated PIC to be present and have a CFM (see general comments for details)
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 Plastic cups were being used as scoops in yogurt parfait topping and bulk sugar bin. Cups were removed and discarded. Use of proper scoops and avoiding bare hand contact with ready to eat foods was discussed. 
Except when washing fruits and vegetables or when ingredients will be added to food that is being fully cooked/has a kill step for pathogens, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Mold and dust were observed inside the ice machine. Dust along the top of the ice maker cover was chunky enough to potentially fall in the ice. Streaks of condensation were passing over mold on the walls, especially in the back of the machine, Areas of significant/immediate concern were wiped down with sanitizer solution during inspection. A layer of ice was removed and discarded after wiping down surfaces inside the machine. Cleaning and maintenance of ice machine were discussed. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 & 4-702.11  Quat solution at 3 part sink was at 0ppm, and a serving utensil was observed in the solution. Utensil was removed and placed with other dirty dishes to go through ware washing process again. Old sanitizer solution was emptied and new solution prepared at 200ppm.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Change out sanitizer solutions frequently/as needed throughout the operating day. Maintain solutions at 200-400ppm as indicated on label directions, and use test strips to verify concentration. 
Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Surfaces inside ice machine had buildup of mold and dust. Areas of immediate concern were addressed during inspection (see #15 for details). Other surfaces remain to be cleaned and sanitized. Cleaning and maintenance of ice machine were discussed. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.citation_text:
3-501.19 Milks, half and half, and whipped topping were observed out for use and time was not marked on products. Milks and half and half were said to be removed at 1pm, and whipped topping was removed at 2pm. Later new containers of milk and half and half were observed in use without time indicated. Proper labeling was discussed for time controlled products, and time was marked on items in use during inspection. Ensure time is written on products as soon as they are removed from cold holding for use. 
NOTE: Any items out for use that are not labeled with time in the future will be discarded. 
If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours food shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time frame for use and cannot exceed 4 hours.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-201.11 Three chemical spray bottles were stored with coffee beans. Two bottles were in a crate with packages, and the other bottle was hanging on the outside of the crate with nozzle facing toward packages. All bottles were moved to the back of facility under personal item storage. Ensure proper storage of all chemicals regardless of ingredients in products used. 
Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, single service and single use articles by separating toxic materials by spacing or partitioning and locating toxic materials in an area that is not above or intermixed with food, equipment, utensils, linens, single service and single use articles.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6501.111 Approximately a half dozen fruit flies were observed under the 3 part sink. The floor drain was observed to be heavily soiled down inside, and some ponding water was observed near the 3 part sink. These conditions are likely contributing to harborage, and effort needs to be made to clean and minimize water which can serve as food and water sources for pests. 
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence eliminating harborage conditions.
NOTE: Fly strips may be placed under the 3 part sink/near the floor drain. However, thorough cleaning is needed in addition to use of traps.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Puddling liquid with little bits of debris were observed in the bottom of the ice scoop holder. Liquid was emptied from the holder during inspection. Ensure ice scoop and holder are cleaned and sanitized at minimum at the end of daily operations and any time contamination may have occurred. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils, such as ice scoops, shall be stored in a clean, protected location.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Coffee filters were out on top of bean grinder upon arrival of inspector. Filters were placed back in original packaging for storage.
Gift cards were observed stored in the same container as plastic spoons and touching the edges of some spoons. Gift cards were removed from the container. 
Proper storage of single use/single service articles was discussed. 
Single service and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not available for use in front service area upon arrival of inspector. Sanitizer solution was prepared (200-400ppm quat). Ensure sanitizer solutions are always available during hours of prep and service for wiping surfaces.
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Floor drain under 3 part sink is heavily soiled down inside with buildup of mold and debris. Drain needs to be thoroughly cleaned and maintained clean to help minimize potential food source for flies and other pests.
Floor in the restroom on the left side of the mopsink was heavily soiled with general buildup. 
Walls in the restroom at the mopsink were observed with holes and gaps around pipes. Repair the walls and seal around pipes. 
Wall behind washer/dryer and handsink had areas of disrepair and spots where gaps were present along drywall seams. Repair and seal the wall.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.06 Employee did not have proof of food handler certification. A laminated list of certified food handlers was posted at the handsink but said to be old/inaccurate.
All staff that are not certified food managers need to have food handler certifications, and copies of food handler certifications need to be maintained on-site.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
750.110g - Prepackaged baked goods for retail sale did not have proper labeling. Labeling requirements were discussed during pre-opening process with Food Program Supervisor. Manager is in the process of creating laminated cards that will be available for reference by the next routine inspection.

Every food pre-packaged in advance of retail sale must bear the following information in English on its label: common name;, address, zip code of the manufacturer, processor, packer, preparer, or distributor; net contents of package; a list of ingredients by their common or usual name; and a list of any artificial color, flavor, or preservative used.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Western tarts that contain diced ham were observed in the fridge with prep date of November 6. Last day to use or discard would have been November 12. Manager pulled product for discard.
Ziplock bag of diced ham in a storage fridge also had no date mark. Manager stated it would have been diced on November 12. Ham would be portioned into tarts for baking later today. Make sure the date of November 12 is used for date mark since ham was diced on that date and not today's date, which is the date or assembly.

Refrigerated foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be clearly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Employee was observed bagging muffins without first washing hands after working the cash register. Employee was also later observed touching the garbage bag to close it and did not wash hands prior to returning to drive thru window to take an order. 
Handwashing between tasks and proper handwashing technique were discussed with staff.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time they may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service items.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - A dead end water line is present in the back half of the building. Removal of this line was discussed with the Food Program Supervisor during the pre-opening process. Manager on duty spoke with the new owner during the inspection and verified a company has been hired to come and remove the water line before the next routine inspection.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Floor drain under the 3 part sink and floor around the drain were soiled with buildup. Approximately a half dozen fruit flies were observed in the area (see general comments for additional details).
Clean the floor drain and the floor under the 3 part sink daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris, which can serve as a food source for pests.

Floors shall be maintained clean.
